title: The Metacyclic Upper Bound |Gal(Xⁿ−p)| ≤ n·φ(n): Pinning |Gal(X⁵−p)| = 20 = |F₂₀| for Every Prime p
description: Supplies the missing ceiling of the metacyclic divisibility bracket and resolves the first open question of the parent boundary entry. The splitting field L of Xⁿ−p over ℚ is generated by a single root α together with a primitive n-th root of unity ζ: every root β satisfies (β/α)ⁿ = 1, hence β/α = ζⁱ is a power of ζ, so β = ζⁱ·α ∈ ℚ(ζ, α). Therefore L = ℚ(ζ)(α), giving the tower ℚ ⊆ ℚ(ζ) ⊆ ℚ(ζ)(α) = L with [ℚ(ζ):ℚ] = φ(n) and [L:ℚ(ζ)] ≤ n (because α is a root of the degree-n polynomial Xⁿ−p already over ℚ(ζ), so its minimal polynomial there has degree ≤ n). Multiplying the tower degrees gives gal_card_le_n_mul_totient: |Gal(Xⁿ−p/ℚ)| = [L:ℚ] ≤ n·φ(n), for every n ≥ 2 and prime p — UNCONDITIONALLY, with no genericity or linear-disjointness hypothesis. This replaces the weak symmetric-group bound |Gal| ∣ n! with the metacyclic ceiling, strictly sharper whenever n·φ(n) < n! (n ≥ 4). Combined with the parent's coprime lower bound n·φ(n) ∣ |Gal| (valid when gcd(n,φ(n)) = 1), gal_card_eq_n_mul_totient_of_coprime pins |Gal(Xⁿ−p/ℚ)| = n·φ(n) EXACTLY at every coprime degree, for every prime p. The headline instance gal_card_quintic_eq_twenty gives |Gal(X⁵−p/ℚ)| = 20 = |F₂₀| = |AGL(1,5)| for every prime p: gcd(5,φ(5)) = gcd(5,4) = 1 forces 20 ∣ |Gal|, the ceiling forces |Gal| ≤ 20, and the factorial bound |Gal| ∣ 120 alone could never close this (20 < 120) — exactly the case the parent left open. 1 theorem, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: The parent chain establishes a two-sided divisibility bracket on the order of the metacyclic Galois group of $X^n-p$: the lower factors $n \mid |\mathrm{Gal}|$ and $\varphi(n) \mid |\mathrm{Gal}|$ (combining to $n\,\varphi(n) \mid |\mathrm{Gal}|$ when $\gcd(n,\varphi(n)) = 1$), against the symmetric-group upper bound $|\mathrm{Gal}| \mid n!$. The deepest parent entry showed the bracket pins the order exactly only at $n = 2, 3$, where $n\,\varphi(n) = n!$ closes the squeeze. For $n \ge 4$ the factorial bound has genuine slack ($n\,\varphi(n) < n!$), so the order was left open — the conjectured value $n\,\varphi(n)$ (the order of the holomorph $\mathbb{Z}/n \rtimes (\mathbb{Z}/n)^\times$) needed a sharper ceiling than $n!$.
overview.problemStatement: Supply the matching upper bound $|\mathrm{Gal}(X^n-p/\mathbb{Q})| \le n\,\varphi(n)$ via the radical tower $\mathbb{Q} \subseteq \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_n) \subseteq \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_n)(\sqrt[n]{p})$, sharp where the $S_n$ bound is loose (e.g. $n = 5$, where $5\,\varphi(5) = 20 < 120 = 5!$), and use it to pin $|\mathrm{Gal}| = n\,\varphi(n)$ exactly at coprime degrees for every prime $p$.
overview.proofStrategy: (1) Generation: the splitting field $L$ contains a primitive $n$-th root of unity $\zeta$ (built from the $n$ distinct ratios $\beta/\alpha$ of the roots of $X^n-p$). Every root $\beta$ satisfies $(\beta/\alpha)^n = 1$, so by IsPrimitiveRoot.eq_pow_of_pow_eq_one $\beta/\alpha = \zeta^i$, whence $\beta = \zeta^i\,\alpha \in \mathbb{Q}(\zeta,\alpha)$. Since the roots generate $L$ (IsSplittingField.adjoin_rootSet) and each lies in $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta,\alpha)$, we get $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta)(\alpha) = L$ (via adjoin_adjoin_left collapsing the relative adjoin). (2) Tower degrees: $[\mathbb{Q}(\zeta):\mathbb{Q}] = \deg \Phi_n = \varphi(n)$ (adjoin.finrank + cyclotomic), and $[L:\mathbb{Q}(\zeta)] = (\mathrm{minpoly}_{\mathbb{Q}(\zeta)}\alpha).\mathrm{natDegree} \le n$ because $\alpha$ is a root of the degree-$n$ polynomial $X^n - p$ over $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta)$ (minpoly.dvd + natDegree_le_of_dvd). (3) Multiply: $|\mathrm{Gal}| = [L:\mathbb{Q}] = [\mathbb{Q}(\zeta):\mathbb{Q}]\,[L:\mathbb{Q}(\zeta)] \le \varphi(n)\,n$ (Module.finrank_mul_finrank). (4) Exact pin: when $\gcd(n,\varphi(n)) = 1$, the parent coprime bound $n\,\varphi(n) \mid |\mathrm{Gal}|$ meets this ceiling (Nat.le_of_dvd + le_antisymm). (5) Instantiate $n = 5$: $\gcd(5,4) = 1$ gives $|\mathrm{Gal}(X^5-p)| = 20$.
keyInsights: **The metacyclic ceiling, unconditionally**: $|\mathrm{Gal}(X^n-p/\mathbb{Q})| \le n\,\varphi(n)$ holds for EVERY $n \ge 2$ and prime $p$, with no genericity or linear-disjointness hypothesis. The splitting field is generated by just two elements — one radical $\alpha = \sqrt[n]{p}$ and one root of unity $\zeta_n$ — so its degree is at most the product of the two cyclic degrees $n$ and $\varphi(n)$, never the full $n!$.

**One root plus one root of unity generate everything**: the crux is that all $n$ roots $\beta$ of $X^n-p$ are $\zeta_n$-multiples of a single root $\alpha$ (since $(\beta/\alpha)^n = 1$ makes $\beta/\alpha$ a power of $\zeta_n$). This collapses the splitting field to $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_n, \alpha)$ and is what bounds the upper tower factor by $n$ instead of $n!$.

**The ceiling meets the floor at coprime degrees**: when $\gcd(n, \varphi(n)) = 1$ the coprime lower bound $n\,\varphi(n) \mid |\mathrm{Gal}|$ and this upper bound $|\mathrm{Gal}| \le n\,\varphi(n)$ squeeze the order to exactly $n\,\varphi(n)$ — for every prime $p$, with no resolvent or embedding argument. This works at every coprime degree, including those ($n \ge 4$) where the factorial squeeze of the parent entry fails.

**$X^5-p$ has Galois group $F_{20} = \mathrm{AGL}(1,5)$ uniformly**: $|\mathrm{Gal}(X^5-p/\mathbb{Q})| = 20$ for EVERY prime $p$. The symmetric-group bound alone is useless here — it only gives $|\mathrm{Gal}| \mid 120$, leaving $20, 40, 60, 120$ open — so the cyclotomic ceiling $|\mathrm{Gal}| \le 20$ is essential. This is the first genuinely-new exact pin beyond the parent's $n = 2, 3$ factorial squeeze, exhibiting the Frobenius affine group $F_{20}$ as the quintic radical Galois group.

**Why the order factors as exactly $n\,\varphi(n)$ — the two-layer normal tower**: the tower $\mathbb{Q} \subseteq \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_n) \subseteq L$ stacks the *abelian cyclotomic* layer $\mathrm{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_n)/\mathbb{Q}) \cong (\mathbb{Z}/n)^\times$ of order $\varphi(n)$ beneath the *radical Kummer* layer $\mathrm{Gal}(L/\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_n)) \hookrightarrow \mathbb{Z}/n$ of order dividing $n$. Since $L/\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_n)$ is normal (a Kummer extension over a base already containing all $n$-th roots of unity), the radical layer is a *normal subgroup* with quotient a subgroup of $(\mathbb{Z}/n)^\times$, exhibiting $\mathrm{Gal}(X^n-p/\mathbb{Q})$ as a metacyclic extension inside the holomorph $\mathbb{Z}/n \rtimes (\mathbb{Z}/n)^\times$. The ceiling $|\mathrm{Gal}| \le n\,\varphi(n)$ is precisely the statement that neither cyclic layer can overshoot its bound; the *product* form $n \cdot \varphi(n)$ (rather than something smaller) is attained exactly when the two layers are linearly disjoint — which coprimality $\gcd(n,\varphi(n)) = 1$ forces, since a common subquotient would violate the coprime orders.

sections.title: The quintic witness |Gal(X⁵−p)| = 20 = |F₂₀|
sections.summary: Proves gal_card_quintic_eq_twenty by instantiating the imported coprime pin at n = 5 (gcd(5,4) = 1, 5·φ(5) = 20), yielding |Gal(X⁵−p/ℚ)| = 20 = |AGL(1,5)| for every prime p. conclusion.summary: Supplied the unconditional metacyclic ceiling |Gal(Xⁿ−p/ℚ)| ≤ n·φ(n) for every n ≥ 2 and prime p, by showing the splitting field L = ℚ(ζₙ)(ⁿ√p) is generated by one radical and one root of unity, giving the tower [L:ℚ] = [ℚ(ζₙ):ℚ]·[L:ℚ(ζₙ)] ≤ φ(n)·n. This replaces the loose symmetric-group bound |Gal| ∣ n! with the sharp metacyclic ceiling. Combined with the parent's coprime lower bound, it pins |Gal(Xⁿ−p/ℚ)| = n·φ(n) exactly at every coprime degree — uniformly in p — and in particular gives |Gal(X⁵−p/ℚ)| = 20 = |F₂₀| for every prime p, the first exact pin beyond the n = 2, 3 factorial squeeze. 1 theorem, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.
conclusion.implications: Closes the metacyclic order bracket from above and resolves the parent entry's first open question. The coprime pin n·φ(n) = |Gal| now holds at every degree with gcd(n,φ(n)) = 1 (n = 2,3,5,7,9,11,...), not just where the factorial squeeze succeeds (n = 2,3). The remaining frontier is the non-coprime case (e.g. n = 4, gcd(4,2) = 2, where the lower bound only gives lcm(4,2) = 4 ∣ |Gal| ≤ 8) and the genuine prime-dependence of |Gal(Xⁿ−p)| at degrees where ℚ(ⁿ√p) and ℚ(ζₙ) fail to be linearly disjoint.
openQuestions: Pin the non-coprime degrees: when gcd(n, φ(n)) > 1 the lower bound drops to lcm(n, φ(n)) ∣ |Gal| ≤ n·φ(n), leaving a gap (e.g. n = 4: 4 ∣ |Gal| ≤ 8). Determine |Gal(Xⁿ−p)| exactly there, recovering the base entry's |Gal(X⁴−2)| = 8 from the ceiling plus an extra linear-disjointness or ramification input.

Characterize when the ceiling |Gal| ≤ n·φ(n) is NOT attained — i.e. the degrees and primes for which ℚ(ⁿ√p) ∩ ℚ(ζₙ) ≠ ℚ, making [L:ℚ(ζₙ)] < n strictly. This is the precise locus where |Gal(Xⁿ−p)| genuinely depends on the prime p.

Identify the semidirect-product structure Gal(Xⁿ−p/ℚ) ≅ ℤ/n ⋊ (ℤ/n)ˣ explicitly at the coprime degrees where the order is now pinned to n·φ(n), upgrading the order equality to a group isomorphism with the holomorph.
